newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX retreats 0.65 pct as high-caps dip.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX retreats 0.65 pct as high-caps dip.

text.p: The BUX index lost 0.65 percent on Friday due to some speculation but most Hungarian shares were adrift in the absence of either market-moving news or significant orders, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 7,396.22 points, down 48.02 points or 0.65 percent.
"Activity was average and most of it was guesswork as there was no news and no orders," said Zsolt Madacsi of ING Barings.
The only notable exception was the usually illiquid home improvements manufacturer Graboplast, which put on 500 forints to close at a record high of 10,700.
"A number of large brokerages were on the buying side," Madacsi said.

OTP Bank gave up 95 forints to end at 6,500 after Hungarian brokerage firm New York Broker Budapest (NYBB) downgraded it to short-term "sell" from "speculative buy" and to long-term "hold" from "buy", on technical grounds.
Madacsi saw no direct link between the rating and the share price movement and said it was rather due to selling orders.
Furniture trading company Domus surged 130 forints to 690 and as the rise exceeded the 20 percent daily increase, was suspended for the last three minutes.
Heavyweight chemicals MOL edged 35 forints lower to 4,290, TVK lost 65 forints to finish at 3,820 while Borsodchem gained 110 forints to finish at 7,500.
Both major pharma shares were also among moderate losers as Richter closed at 17,720, down 240 and Egis ended at 12,900, down 100.
However, traders said that a strong dollar could push Hungarian shares higher on Monday.
"If the dollar preserves its strength until Monday, Budapest stocks will climb again," Madacsi said.
